newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish consumption rise may hit economy - minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish consumption rise may hit economy - minister.

text.p: Poland's economic reforms and growth may be jeopardised if individual consumption, up about 10 percent last year, continues at the same pace in 1997, Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said on Tuesday.
Kaczmarek told a news conference that wages growth should be curbed to contain domestic demand or the foreign trade deficit will balloon beyond reasonable levels and undermine economic expansion.
"If the consumption growth is maintained, this may pose a threat to our reforms," he said. @

"Companies' management ought to be disciplined as far as wage policy is concerned. We have witnessed a clear increase of domestic demand, which resulted from a six-percent real wage rise in 1996," he added.

The government has no say over wages in private firms but it can influence salaries in state-owned companies, which are set on an annual basis during negotiations in the so-called Trilateral Commission, a body of government, trade unions and employers' group representatives. @

Kaczmarek did not say whether and how the government would curb wage rise. Analysts say the ruling leftist coalition was unlikely to try to radically push it down ahead of parliamentary elections, scheduled for around September.
On Monday, Finance Minister Marek Belka said the economy could overheat if quick growth of domestic demand is coupled with fast growth of wages.
Earlier this year, the independent central bank increased obligatory reserve requirements and kept nominal interest rates flat ,despite falling inflation, to cool domestic demand.
